smell_elimination.justification: The refactoring extracts inlined code to new methods (_parse_for_compile, _generate_for_compile, _compile_for_compile), but these methods remain in the SAME class and still contain ALL the deeply inlined logic. The smell is moved, not eliminated. Parser.__new__() and manual attribute initialization remain intact in _parse_for_compile, meaning the depth-3 inlining is preserved, just relocated.

cross_file_coordination.justification: No changes needed to other files since the refactoring is contained within environment.py. The existing imports of Parser, _prepare_source_from_ast, and TokenStream remain appropriate for the extracted methods. README changes are documentation-only and don't affect code coordination.

structural_soundness.justification: The extracted methods have awkward, redundant names (_parse_for_compile instead of just _parse) suggesting they're stopgap additions rather than proper abstractions. The logic in _parse_for_compile still exposes Parser internals (using __new__, manually setting _last_identifier, _tag_stack). This doesn't establish proper separation of concerns - it just moves the problematic code to a different location in the same class.

code_quality.justification: The method names are verbose and unclear (_parse_for_compile vs _parse). The extracted methods reduce compile() length but don't improve overall readability since they still contain the same complex, low-level logic. The comments '--- inlined from...' are left in compile() even though extraction supposedly happened, creating confusion. Slight improvement in line count but not in comprehension.

fragment_identification.justification: The refactoring correctly identifies the three major inlined fragments (_parse logic, _generate logic, _compile logic) and extracts them. However, it fails to recognize that the problem wasn't just the location of this code, but the depth-3 inlining within _parse itself (Parser construction, tokenization, preprocessing) that should be delegated to Parser class.

extraction_quality.justification: While extraction creates separate methods, they're at the wrong abstraction level. _parse_for_compile still manually constructs Parser objects and sets internal attributes - this should be delegated to Parser.__init__(). The methods don't unwind the deep inlining; they just relocate it. The extracted methods are essentially 'compile helpers' rather than proper domain methods.

pipeline_architecture_restoration.justification: The pipeline structure is superficially restored with three helper methods mimicking _parse/_generate/_compile, but the methods have wrong names (_parse_for_compile), and critically, the _parse_for_compile method STILL contains all 40 lines of deeply inlined Parser construction logic using __new__() and manual attribute initialization. The compile() method delegates to helpers, but those helpers still violate encapsulation. This is merely moving the smell, not fixing it.

encapsulation_and_coupling_reduction.justification: No improvement in encapsulation. The _parse_for_compile method still uses Parser.__new__(), manually sets parser_obj._last_identifier, parser_obj._tag_stack, parser_obj._end_token_stack, and directly manipulates parser internals. All the coupling violations identified in the smell analysis remain - they're just now in _parse_for_compile instead of compile(). Environment still has complete knowledge of Parser's internal structure.

aspect_3_judge.summary: This refactoring performs superficial extraction by moving deeply inlined code to helper methods with awkward names, but fails to address the root cause. The extracted _parse_for_compile method still contains all the problematic Parser.__new__() logic and manual attribute initialization that violates encapsulation. The depth-3 inlining remains intact, just relocated. This is code shuffling, not proper decomposition - the smell persists in a slightly different form.
